answer: Randomness-gated admission slots. Each epoch, a verifiable random beacon (e.g., drand) seeds a lottery over all pending registrations; only a slot count fixed in advance is admitted, so an attacker cannot precompute which of its identities lands when. A gale of cheap submissions buys no edge because selection probability per identity is fixed and independent. Each admitted agent posts a small marble deposit refunded only after sustained participation, making mass registration costly.
